edges.label: The 38-title list is the only official enumeration of the series
edges.note: DIA released the list to Steven Aftergood of FAS on 16 January 2019 under FOIA; it had been provided to Congress in January 2018. Without this release the series would be known only from leaks.

a.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)

edges.label: deliverable under AAWSAP
edges.note: Tier 2, and the reason is worth stating. A full-text scan of this released DIRD on 23 August 2026 found NO occurrence of the programme name anywhere in the document - unlike 27 of the 32 scanned, whose inside cover names the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program explicitly. The link therefore rests on the DIA's 9 January 2018 list to the Senate Armed Services Committee, which enumerates it among the 38 reference products, and not on the document's own text.

edges.label: authored

b.label: The Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research

edges.label: author of record on the DIA list
edges.note: DIA list item 10: "Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research, Dr George Hathaway, Hathaway Consulting." This is the attribution most likely to be got wrong from the title alone: the paper reviews the Podkletnov and Ning Li gravity-modification claims but was not written by either of them or by any academic advocate of the effect. It was written by the Toronto engineer who had run the Podkletnov replication and reported null results.

edges.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records entry 9 as 'High Frequency Gravitational Wave Communications, Dr Robert Baker, GravWave' - the earlier KLAS transcription rendered the title as 'Gravity Wave Communication'. The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Baker confirmed to researcher Keith Basterfield that he published three related HFGW papers in 2010.

edges.label: authored by George H. Miley, University of Illinois
edges.note: Entry 1 on both the KLAS list of July 2018 and the DIA letter of 9 January 2018: 'Inertial Electrostatics Confinement Fusion, Dr George Miley, Univ. of Illinois.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(5). Miley is co-author of the Springer monograph on IEC fusion, making him a documented subject-matter authority rather than a fringe recruit.

edges.label: authored by Ulf Leonhardt, University of St Andrews
edges.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Invisibility Cloaking, Dr Ulf Leonhardt, Univ of St Andrews.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Leonhardt had been publishing on transformation optics and cloaking since 2006 and was, by the ICOD of 1 December 2009, one of the small number of internationally recognised authorities in the field. George Knapp released a copy of the DIRD in February 2019.

a.label: Ultracapacitors as Energy and Power Storage Devices for Commercial and Military Applications

edges.label: author's affiliation of record; one of three Lockheed Martin DIRDs
edges.note: Lockheed Martin appears three times on the DIA list: this paper, Dr V Teofilo's "Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion," and Dr S Macheret's MHD air-breathing propulsion paper. Eric Davis said in a June 2018 interview that the advanced nuclear fusion for aerospace propulsion work was done by colleagues at Lockheed Martin, which matches the list. This is a direct, documented thread from the DIRD series into the prime-contractor cluster.

edges.label: authored
edges.note: DIA list item 23 names "Dr W McCarthy, Programmable Matter Corporation". Released PDF redacts the author under (b)(6).

edges.label: authored (attribution by elimination, see note)
edges.note: TIER 2 AND DELIBERATELY SO. The DIA list establishes at tier 1 that two aneutronic fusion DIRDs exist, one by V. Teofilo (Lockheed Martin) and one by W. Culbreth (UNLV). Which released document number belongs to which author is NOT stated on either cover, both of which redact the author under (b)(6). This document, DIA-08-1011-003, is assigned to Culbreth because the companion DIA-08-1011-004 carries a V. Teofilo self-citation at endnote 17 and Lockheed Martin content, while this one carries none of either and is instead saturated with Nevada Test Site, Project Rover and NERVA material plus nuclear engineering textbook citations. If the mapping is ever shown to be reversed, this edge and its partner must be swapped together.
